Definition: from G3441; to isolate, i.e. bereave:--be desolate.
BiblicalUsage: Monoo means to leave desolate, to bereave — Paul's true widow is the woman left alone, desolate, who trusts in God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day. In the Greek text the form stands under the lemma μονόομαι, spelled differently from this study's headword.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the desolate widow is the church's charge precisely because she has no one else: God counts her prayers as her standing.
